title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is formulating fixed-point forms of the section conjecture (early 1980s, around La Longue Marche). Conjecture B, on the preceding pages, concerns a Galois group Gamma = Gal(K̄|K) acting semilinearly on the profinite universal cover U of a hyperbolic curve. That action normalises the geometric fundamental group pi. Its fixed points on the completion Û (the profinite universal cover with cusps added) should correspond to rational points or cusps. On the previous page he strengthens this: Gamma^0 = ker(chi: Gamma -> Ẑ*), the kernel of the cyclotomic character, should already have exactly one fixed point. This gives pi^{Gamma^0} = 1 at finite fixed points and pi^{Gamma^0} = L_i (an inertia/cusp subgroup) at a fixed point at infinity.

This page draws two consequences and sets up the next conjecture.

(1) Base field. If only Gamma^0 matters, the statements should hold not only for K finitely generated over Q. They should also hold for K finitely generated over a cyclotomic field, possibly infinite over Q, e.g. Q(mu_infinity). Gamma^0 is exactly the absolute Galois group of K(mu_infinity).

(2) Poincaré curves. Over an algebraically closed field K̄ of characteristic 0 he defines a 'courbe de Poincaré' as anything isomorphic to the (pro-)universal covering of an algebraic curve over K̄. Two curves U, V define isomorphic Poincaré covers iff some finite étale cover of one is isomorphic to some finite étale cover of the other. So a Poincaré curve is the profinite universal cover, which retains only the commensurability class of the curve.

(3) Completion. Each Poincaré curve has a canonical completion Û: the inverse limit of the smooth compactifications of the finite levels, adding cusps. It is functorial for all automorphisms of the pair (Ũ, K̄), including those that act nontrivially on K̄ (semilinear automorphisms).

This prepares Conjecture B' on the next page. Take any action of Gamma on a Poincaré curve over K̄ that is compatible with the action on K̄. Such an action need not come from a model of any finite level over K, and need not normalise a given pi. Then Gamma^0 has exactly one fixed point on Û. This is a commensurability-invariant, 'model-free' section conjecture, stated for the cyclotomic-kernel subgroup.
errors: The equivalence criterion (common finite étale cover) is the right notion of commensurability for the profinite universal cover. Implicitly the curves must be hyperbolic, or at least anabelian, for the later conjectures. Also, 'universal cover' must be read as the pro-universal (profinite) cover, i.e. a pro-scheme, not an actual curve.

The extension to fields finitely generated over Q(mu_infinity) is heuristic. Several known tools are unavailable over such fields, which are not sub-p-adic and have infinitely ramified places: the injectivity of points into sections via Kummer theory needs, e.g., finiteness of torsion and absence of divisible elements in Jacobians over K(mu_infinity) (Ribet-type results). No argument is given here.

ideas.what: Fixed-point (on the completed profinite universal cover) formulation of the section conjecture, including cusps as 'fixed points at infinity'
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture, fixed-point / pro-universal-cover form (with cuspidal sections)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, letter to Faltings (1983); developed by Nakamura, Tamagawa, Stix
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 1983 (in Geometric Galois Actions I, 1997)

ideas.what: Strengthening to Gamma^0 = ker of the cyclotomic character, hence to base fields finitely generated over cyclotomic (possibly infinite) extensions of Q
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture over K(mu_infinity) / fields containing all roots of unity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not standard; anabelian results are usually proved for finitely generated or sub-p-adic fields

ideas.what: 'Courbes de Poincaré': profinite universal covers of algebraic curves over K̄, classified up to commensurability (common finite étale cover)
ideas.modern_name: Commensurability class of a curve / pro-universal cover as an object in its own right
ideas.usually_credited_to: Commensurability ideas are classical (arithmetic groups); profinite-cover viewpoint is in anabelian geometry, e.g. Mochizuki's work on commensurators

ideas.what: Canonical completion Û of a Poincaré curve, functorial for semilinear automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Compactified profinite universal cover (pro-system of smooth compactifications with cusps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in anabelian literature (e.g. Stix's book on rational points and fundamental groups)

missed.claim: A section-conjecture variant where the hypothesis is only a semilinear Galois action on the pro-universal cover, determined only up to commensurability. No normalised pi, no model over K required. The conclusion is a unique Gamma^0-fixed point, over bases finitely generated over cyclotomic fields. This 'model-free, commensurability-invariant, cyclotomic-kernel' form does not appear as a standard conjecture in the anabelian literature.
missed.quote: tous nos beaux énoncés devraient être valables ... dès que K est ext. de type fini d'un corps cyclotomique (pas néc. fini sur Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Anabelian geometry over fields containing mu_infinity (e.g. Q^ab-type fields) is largely unexplored. The formulation suggests a commensurability-class version of the section conjecture relevant to questions on Q-curve-like 'virtually defined over K' objects.

missed.claim: Explicit notion of 'Poincaré curve' over K̄: the profinite universal cover modulo commensurability, with a canonical completion functorial for semilinear automorphisms. This appears as a named object in Grothendieck's program.
missed.quote: Nous pourrions définir les courbes de Poincaré ... comme étant les courbes isomorphes aux revêtements universels de courbes alg. sur K̄
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates treating the commensurability class (and its semilinear automorphisms) as the basic anabelian object, akin to later commensurator studies (Mochizuki).

deep.surprise_reason: The fixed-point form of the section conjecture is known from the Faltings letter. The specific Gamma^0 strengthening is less familiar: it extends to fields finitely generated over infinite cyclotomic fields. So is the model-free 'Poincaré curve' formulation. Both are notable unpublished details, but they are conjectural sketches rather than results.
